[[Category:Probability theory| 2]]
A '''probability space''' is a [[measure space]] built on a [[sample space]] and a '''probability measure'''.

== Definition ==

Let $\Omega$ be a [[sample space]] and let $\mathcal F(\Omega)$ be a [[sigma-algebra]] on $\Omega$. 

=== Probability measure ===

A '''probability measure''' is a special [[measure space#Measure|measure]] satisfying the '''normalisation condition''':

$$
P:\mathcal F(\Omega) \to [0,1] \\
P(\Omega)=1
$$

=== Probability space ===

$$
(\Omega,\mathcal{F}(\Omega),P)
$$

is a '''probability space''', and $E \in \mathcal{F}(\Omega)$ are '''events''' of the sample space $\Omega$, whose probabilities can be measured.
